texts.preamble: Sh. Sanjay S/O. Late Sh. Ved Prakash vs Sh. Jai Singh on 5 January, 2016 In The Court Of Ms. Ravinder Bedi : Presiding Officer, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal : Karkardooma Courts : East District : Delhi Mac No. : 209 Of 2012 Unique Case I.D. No. : 02402C0 252252012 1. Sh. Sanjay S/o. Late Sh. Ved Prakash R/o. H.No. 486, Gali No. 17, Budh Vihar, Mandoli, Delhi. ... Petitioner Versus 1. Sh. Jai Singh, S/o. Sh. Rattan Singh C/o. Ps Janakpuri, Delhi.
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed the present claim petition under section 166 & 140 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.03.2012. The facts as setup by the petitioner in his petition are that on 27.03.2012 at about 9.15 pm while he was going on his Motorcycle, he was hit by a Car make Ambassador bearing registration no. DL 1CJ5552 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), from behind, which was driven by its driver at a high speed and rash manner. He fell down and sustained injuries and was taken to LBS Hospital. A case was registered against the Respondent no. 1 vide FIR no. 89/12, PS Pandav Nagar u/s. 279/338 IPC . 3. It is stated by the Petitioner that the Respondent no.1 is the Driver and Respondent no.2 is the Sh. Sanjay S/O. Late Sh. Ved Prakash vs Sh. Jai Singh on 5 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54154989/ 1 Owner and they both are jointly and severally liable to make the payment of compensation to the Petitioner. 4. The Respondent no. 1 in his Written Statement has stated that the petitioner himself was negligent while driving his motorcycle in a zig zag manner without caring for safety rules; that the injured was taken to LBS Hospital by Responent no. 1 in the offending vehicle. The Respondent no. 2 in his Written Statement has also taken the same contentions. 5. On the basis of pleadings, following issues were framed vide order dated 08.11.2013 : Petitioner suffered injuries in road side accident on 27.03.2012 involving vehicle i.e. Car bearing registration no. DL1CJ5552 being driven allegedly in a rash and negligent manner by R 1? 2. To what amount of compensation, if any, the MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 2/13 Petitioner is entitled to and from whom? 3. Relief. 6. Petitioner examined himself as PW1 and filed his affidavit as Ex. PW1/A. He proved the documents i.e., DAR as Ex. PW1/1, Medical Bills as Ex. PW1/2, Treatment Record as Ex. PW1/3, his Driving License as Ex. PW1/4, Disability Certificate as Ex. PW1/5 Salary Slips as Ex. PW1/6,Documents verified by IO as Ex. PW1/7. PW2 Dr. Amit Pankaj, Professor (Orthopaedics) from GTB Hospital, proved the Disability Certificate as Ex.PW1/5 mentioning 29% permanent disability in relation to right upper & right lower limb suffered by the Petitioner. 7. It is pertinent to mention that Respondents have not brought any evidence in support of their contentions. PW1 testified that on 27.03.2012 at about 9.15 pm, he was going on his Motorcycle when he was hit by a Car make Ambassador bearing registration no. DL1CJ5552 from behind. He testified that the offending vehicle was driven in rash and negligent manner and rammed into his motorcycle. He testified that on account of accident, he sustained serious injuries and the resultant permanent disability.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the respondents argued that the entire petition does not specify the exact manner of the accident. It is argued that Petitioner stated to have been hit by the offending vehicle coming from behind, but the Mechanical Inspection Reports of both vehicles points out contrary to this. It is argued that from the damages sustained by vehicles, it is clear that it was a headon collision in which the Motorcyclist himself rammed against the car. It is argued that the accident happened due to the negligence of motorcyclist himself. It is argued that the driver of the offending car had taken the injured to the Hospital. Ld. Counsel has further pointed out certain discrepancies in the petition, the affidavits as well as the final computation given by the Petitioner in respect of the variance of the amount of compensation sought besides discrepancies in the contents of the Affidavit earlier filed by the Petitioner dated 13.10.2013 and the subsequent Affidavit dated 21.05.2014. Ld. Counsel thus, requests for the deduction of the amount on the basis of the negligence of Petitioner, which contributed to the accident. Ld. Counsel for the Petitioner, MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 4/13 however, argued that the contributory negligence cannot be assumed in the absence of any supporting material having brought by the Respondents. United India Insurance Co. I (2014) ACC 206 SC. I am placing reliance upon the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court in Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand (2011) 11 SCC 635 and Kusum Lata v. Satbir, (2011) 3 SCC 646. 12.In case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310, an adverse inference was drawn because the driver of the offending vehicle had not appeared MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 5/13 in the witness box to corroborate his defence taken in the written statement. In General Manager, Kerala State Road Trans. Corpn. V/s. Susamma Thomas 1994 ACJ 1 (SC), the Apex Court held as under : "(5)........ The determination of the quantum must answer what contemporary society 'would deem MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 6/13 to be a fair sum such as would allow the wrongdoer to hold up his head among his neighbours and say with their approval that he has done the fair thing. The amount awarded must not be niggardly since the law value life and limb in a free society in generous scales' All this means that the sum awarded must be fair and reasonable by accepted legal standards.". 16.In Nizam Institute of medical Sciences V/s. Prasanth S. Dhananka, 2010 ACJ 38 (SC), the Hon'ble Supreme Court emphasized that cases of serious injuries in the motor vehicle accident are worse than the death cases because the victim and his family suffer throughout life. 17.Hon'ble Supreme Court has enumerated the principles for granting compensation payable to road traffic accident victims. In the case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr., MANU/SC/1018/2010, Civil Appeal No. 8981/2010 decided on 18.10.2010, following principles were laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court for determining compensation payable to road traffic accident victims : i) The compensation payable to the Petitioner who is a victim of road accident should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the Petitioner to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equatable manner. ii) Compensation payable in injury cases is payable under two heads. They are pecuniary damages (special damages) and non pecuniary damages. Pecuniary damages have three MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 7/13 sub heads which are : (i) expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) (a) Loss of earning (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising of loss of earning during the period of treatment and (b) loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability (iii) Future medical expenses. Nonpecuniary damages (General Damage) are (iv) damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of injuries (v) loss of amenities and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and (vi) loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). Sh. Sanjay S/O. on 5 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54154989/ 4 iii) From overall MAC NO.209/12 SANJAY V/S. JAI SINGH & ORS. 8/13 circumstances, the functional disability of the Petitioner is taken as 10%, in relation to the whole body, in view of the dictum of "Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343". 19.As So far future prospects concern, in a recent judgment in HDFC Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Lalta Devi & Ors., (Decided on 12.1.2015), it was observed that the three Judge Bench Decision in Reshma Kumari & Ors. Vs. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65 was held to be taken as a binding precedent. 26.A victim of an accident has to be compensated in terms of money even if gratuitous services are rendered by a family member. In Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. Vs. Lalita, AIR 1981 Delhi 558, Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has held that there cannot be any deduction if domestic help is obtained from a family member. This judgment was again relied upon by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Narayan Bahadur v. Sumeet Gupta and Anr., MAC APP. No. 762/11 dated 04.07.12.
